item.text: {"text":"The closest direct precedent is [MTAM (CIKM 2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598): elapsed-time gates modify GRU state transitions, while short-term intent queries historical memory through time-aware attention. This separates recent intent from historical preferences within one jointly trained network. More recent [SAPM (2025 manuscript)](https://cis.temple.edu/~jiewu/research/publications/Publication_files/2025-TWeb-Stability-aware%20Preference%20Modeling%20for%20Sequential%20Recommendation.pdf) introduces multi-head GRU representations and feature-level stability-aware fusion. [ScaleRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457325002596) explicitly models multiple interaction scales using patches and local/global attention; useful motivation for multiscale memory, although its Transformer backbone is outside this experiment’s scope.\n\nA suitable research hypothesis is a single GRU network with fast and slow hidden-state groups, jointly trained item embeddings, and bounded gates conditioned on observed log-transformed inter-event gaps. This is a proposed adaptation, not an established result from those papers. Compare ordinary GRU gates, one shared exponential decay, fixed fast/slow decay, and learned content-plus-time gates at comparable parameter counts. [TLSRec (CIKM 2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04760) motivates feature-wise temporal fusion rather than a single scalar weight, but uses attention and the lag to prediction time. Here, use only timestamps available at inference; never infer a withheld target timestamp. Assess gains with the fixed macro validation HR@10, and examine whether improvements concentrate in histories with long gaps. Preserve one checkpoint per category and read the final nonpadding state of left-padded histories."}
